recommended_title: When Is One Kernel SHAP Run Enough? Predicting Top-3 Attribution Reproducibility from a Single Budgeted Run
central_question: For a trained tabular classifier explained by a budget-limited Kernel SHAP run, how often does the single run's top-3 feature set agree with independent reruns, and can that agreement be predicted from the single run's own coalition data better than trivial and split-half baselines?
central_thesis: Single-run Kernel SHAP top-3 reproducibility is conditional rather than uniformly high (mean agreement 0.807 at a 4d coalition budget vs 0.932 at 16d on the held-out evaluation datasets), and a diagnostic computed only from the assessed run predicts it with lower squared error than always-reliable, constant-0.5 and split-half-gap baselines, but only modestly above a pairing-permuted control, so most of its skill is budget-level calibration and per-instance resolution is limited (Spearman 0.58).
narrative_rationale: The final evaluation completed with outcome qualified (final.qualification.outcome), with positive lower confidence bounds against all three evaluator baselines and against the permuted-pairing control, so a measured-results paper is supportable. The artifacts do not support the original brief's broad empirical study (no per-dataset/per-model breakdown, no background-size or retraining-noise experiments, no deep tabular models, no ablation_studies). The strongest coherent story is therefore a bounded one: define single-run reproducibility operationally (top-3 Jaccard against 8 reruns), show it depends on coalition budget, and evaluate a single-run self-diagnostic against honest baselines and a control, stating loudly that the gain over the control is small. This is thesis-first and avoids the three-attempt search chronology; search is demoted to a short supplementary robustness note because there are no ablations that attribute the gain to components.

method_groups.name: Single-run reproducibility label (measurement protocol)
method_groups.include_reason: Defines the object being predicted: for each explained instance, mean top-3 Jaccard agreement between the assessed Kernel SHAP run and 8 independent reruns, at coalition budgets 4d and 16d, background 32 rows, three model families (logistic regression, random forest, sklearn MLP). Needed to state the conditional-reliability claim (final.metric.mean_label_low_budget / mean_label_high_budget).

method_groups.name: Single-run self-diagnostic (frozen selected configuration)
method_groups.include_reason: The studied method: from one run's coalition masks, weights and values it simulates reruns via a delete-one-group jackknife (4 partitions, antithetic common-random-number draws), shrinks toward a budget-dependent prior and adds a small margin gate, outputting r_hat in [0,1]. Constants are hand-set and untuned; say so.

method_groups.name: Evaluator-owned reference baselines
method_groups.include_reason: Always-reliable (r=1), constant 0.5, and a split-half-gap heuristic computed from the same single run. Grounded via final.metric.skill_vs_always_reliable, skill_vs_constant_half, skill_vs_gap_heuristic and their CI lows. The original search-time baseline program has no grounded score in paper_data, so that comparison is omitted.

method_groups.name: Label-permuted pairing control
method_groups.include_reason: Shuffles which r_hat is paired with which instance label (20 deterministic derangements) to separate budget/cell-level calibration from instance-specific information. Score 0.9701 vs diagnostic 0.9838 (final.metric.control_permuted_score, combined_minus_control_ci_low). The key calibration guard of the paper.

method_groups.name: Search-plane model variants (three configurations)
method_groups.include_reason: Supplement-only: three scored configurations on search datasets (result.improvement_001..003) show the selection and that differences are small; no component ablations exist, so no mechanistic attribution is claimed. All 3 attempts were scored; there are no unscored attempts.

results_focus: Conditional reliability: final mean label 0.8065 at 4d vs 0.9315 at 16d budget (final.metric.mean_label_low_budget, mean_label_high_budget); single-run top-3 set reproducibility is not uniformly high, and the low-budget regime is where one run is least trustworthy. Do not break this down by dataset or model family; no grounded breakdown exists.

Diagnostic accuracy on final data: combined score 0.9838 (= 1 - mean squared error, so MSE about 0.0162; derived arithmetic, label it derived) with seed-level scores 0.9850 and 0.9826 (final.evidence.episodes, seeds 9001/9002).

Skill over baselines with one-sided 2.5th-percentile bootstrap lower bounds: vs always-reliable +0.0353 (low 0.0171), vs constant 0.5 +0.1543 (low 0.1245), vs split-half gap heuristic +0.0122 (low 0.0081). Only lower bounds are available; do not fabricate upper bounds or symmetric intervals.

Honest control: permuted-pairing score 0.9701; diagnostic minus control = 0.0137 (derived), lower bound 0.0101. Interpret as real but small instance-specific information on top of budget-level calibration; Spearman between r_hat and label 0.581 indicates moderate ranking ability.
Scale of the gain in plain terms: root-mean-squared error about 0.127 for the diagnostic vs about 0.227 for always-reliable (both derived from grounded metrics; label as derived).

Selection is reported separately from the final evaluation: search scores 0.9760, 0.9837, 0.9854 for three scored configurations on the search datasets; the frozen selected configuration is the 0.9854 one. Per-attempt two-seed ranges overlap, so the ordering is not claimed significant.
Final outcome is qualified (final.qualification.outcome); no failed-qualification disclosure needed, but qualification does not turn these bounded metrics into general validity claims.

planned_subsections.heading: Diagnostic constants and their provenance
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Hand-set, untuned constants (budget prior 0.84/0.96 taken from search-plane budget-wise label means, simulation weight 0.6, margin boost 0.02, 4 partitions); the prior was derived from search data whose label means (0.840/0.958) differ from final (0.807/0.932), a likely source of mild miscalibration. Source for numbers is the program notes; flag as method description, not a metric.

notes_for_writer: Stay inside the bounded claim: Kernel SHAP with interventional value function, 32-row background, budgets 4d and 16d, k=3, three model families, three final datasets, 20 instances per episode, 8 reruns. The task brief's broader items (background-size effects, retraining noise, deep tabular models, other explainers, leverage-score estimators) were not run; list them as not done, not as findings.

Present the reproducibility label as the primary scientific object and the diagnostic as the tool evaluated; the title and abstract should name the mechanism (single-run self-diagnostic of Kernel SHAP top-3 reproducibility) and the setting.

Never write combined_score in the paper; call it 'score = 1 - mean squared error of r_hat against the agreement label' and describe aggregation as instance -> seed -> model/budget cell -> dataset equal-weight means.

Uncertainty: only the final seed-level scores (two seeds) and one-sided 2.5th-percentile paired-bootstrap lower bounds exist. Say so. Do not draw error bars the artifacts cannot support; lower bounds can be drawn as markers.
Frame the permuted control as the main limitation-aware result: 0.9701 vs 0.9838 shows most skill is budget/cell-level calibration. State this in the abstract.
The diagnostic's budget prior was set from search-plane label means; final label means are lower, so say miscalibration at the margin is plausible but not measured.
Per-dataset and per-family conclusions are not grounded; do not state any, and name this as a limitation. The 4d vs 16d label gap is an aggregate across datasets and families.

The selected configuration's constants were hand-set and untuned, and diagnostics trust is marked unverified in the evaluation evidence; disclose. No component ablation exists, so do not attribute gains to jackknife, partition ensembling, shrinkage or margin gate individually.
Do not cite the original search-time baseline program's score; it has no grounded source id. Use evaluator-owned baselines instead.
